units.passage: consult the appropriate research or compliance office when a proposed use is unclear. Respect Copyright and Licensed Resources Uploading articles, books, images, course materials, or other protected content to an AI platform may violate copyright, intellectual property, or license requirements. Many library databases and electronic resources are governed by agreements that restrict copying, automated analysis, text and data mining, or use with generative AI. Improper use may jeopardize access to a resource for the entire university community and expose the user or university to legal risk. Before using copyrighted or licensed material with AI: Confirm that the proposed use is permitted. Review the terms governing the source, database, or resource. Determine whether the AI provider may retain or reuse the material. Contact Copley Library if you are unsure whether a resource may be uploaded, analyzed, or mined. Review Copley Library’s Licensed Resources Policy Review the ITS Copyright Infringement Policy When in Doubt, Ask Because AI tools and their uses are changing rapidly, this guidance cannot anticipate every situation. When you are unsure: Ask your instructor about academic use. Review the Approved AI Tools and Data Allowances . Contact Copley Library about licensed resources, citation, copyright, or text and data mining. Consult the appropriate research or compliance office about research-related uses.
units.why: "Consult the appropriate research or compliance office about research-related uses" points to offices for research questions: P115 (point to further guidance).

units.passage: When drafting a syllabus statement on the use of generative AI, you may want to consider and address the following questions: Will I allow the use of generative AI in my course? What are my expectations for students who use generative AI? For what purposes can students use these tools Can they use them for brainstorming? Proofreading? Composing text? How do I define appropriate and ethical usage for generative AI? What are my parameters? What constitutes academic misconduct within my course with respect to the use of generative AI? How will I ensure students are aware of and respect any applicable confidentiality and privacy policies? How will I require students to disclose and/or cite their use of generative AI? Will I create my own guidelines or have them follow APA citation guidelines or MLA citation guidelines ? How will I ensure my students understand their responsibility for AI-generated content? Are there assignments where my expectations differ from the guidelines presented at the beginning of the semester? How will I convey this to students? For more syllabus ideas, see this handout on Sample Syllabi Statements for Generative AI and ChatGPT Usage . In addition to including a statement on the use of generative AI in your syllabus, you might also consider having a conversation with your students about generative AI tools at the beginning of the semester and throughout the semester, as needed, to ensure clarity.
